chapter.title: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard

page.h1: HTS Chapter 47: Pulp of Wood or of Other Fibrous Cellulosic Material; Recovered (Waste and Scrap) Paper or Paperboard — U.S. Export Rules & Ways to Pay Less Abroad

seo.title: U.S. Pulp & Waste Paper Export Rules: Schedule B, EAR99, EEI (HTS Ch. 47) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Schedule B codes for fluff and kraft pulp and OCC, why pulp and waste paper are EAR99 except for Russia and Belarus, AES filing, and how buyers abroad cut what they pay.
keywords: hs code for occ waste paper

intro: A U.S. exporter of wood pulp or recovered paper takes the same five steps as every exporter. No U.S. agency issues an export permit or certificate for pulp or waste paper, and they are **EAR99**, so a licence is needed only for embargoed destinations, restricted parties and **Russia and Belarus**, where every six-digit Chapter 47 code except dissolving pulp is on Commerce's licence list. Recovered paper is not a hazardous waste, so EPA's hazardous-waste export rules do not apply; what decides whether a container of OCC clears is the buyer country's import rules, on the Markets page. The money questions abroad are a Chinese buyer's tariff exclusion, a Canadian buyer's remission of the surtax on dissolving pulp, and, for EU buyers of wood pulp, deforestation due-diligence data from December 30, 2026.

steps.title: Find the Schedule B number
steps.whatToDo: Look up the 10-digit Schedule B number for each product with the Census Bureau's free search tool. Its first six digits are the same as the HS code every country uses, so it also tells you which line of the buyer's tariff applies. The U.S. import (HTS) number and the Schedule B number match only to six digits.
steps.when: Every export. It goes on the export filing (the last step) and on the commercial invoice.
steps.chapterNote: Fluff pulp and other bleached softwood kraft are 4703.21 ($4.33B in 2025), bleached hardwood kraft 4703.29, dissolving pulp 4702.00. Recovered paper is split by grade: OCC and other unbleached kraft or corrugated 4707.10 ($1.52B), white or bleached office grades 4707.20, newspapers and magazines (mainly mechanical pulp) 4707.30, and mixed or unsorted paper 4707.90. Classify to six digits before quoting: Canada surtaxes only 4702, China's 2018 list rates differ by line (5% on wood pulp, 20% on recycled-fiber pulp 4706.20, 25% on recovered paper), and the EU deforestation rules cover wood pulp but not recovered paper.

steps.title: Screen the buyer and everyone in the deal
steps.whatToDo: Check the buyer, the end user and any agent against the Consolidated Screening List. It combines the Commerce lists (Entity List, Denied Persons, Unverified, Military End-User), the State Department lists and the Treasury (OFAC) sanctions lists of parties you may not deal with, or may deal with only under a licence.
steps.when: Every export, before you accept the order.
steps.chapterNote: Recovered paper and market pulp are often sold through brokers and traders to mills in Asia and Latin America; screen the end mill and the final destination, not only the party that places the order.

steps.title: Check whether you need an export licence
steps.whatToDo: Find the product's Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) on the Commerce Control List. Most goods are not listed and are EAR99. For a listed ECCN, look up the destination on the Commerce Country Chart under each reason for control: an X means a licence is needed unless a licence exception applies. Even EAR99 goods need a licence for embargoed countries and for restricted end users or end uses.
steps.when: Every export of goods subject to the Export Administration Regulations (EAR).
steps.chapterNote: Wood pulp and recovered paper are EAR99 and ship without a licence (NLR) to most destinations. The exceptions are set by destination and party, not by product: see the sanctions step.

steps.title: Check sanctions on the destination
steps.whatToDo: Check the destination against OFAC's sanctions programs and the EAR's embargo rules. Cuba, Iran and North Korea have country-wide rules, and Syria still needs a Commerce licence for most items; Russia and Belarus need a licence for any item with an ECCN. Several programs have special permissions for food and medicine.
steps.when: Exports to a sanctioned or embargoed country, or to a listed person anywhere.
steps.chapterNote: Russia and Belarus: Supplement No. 4 to Part 746 lists every six-digit Chapter 47 code except dissolving pulp (4702.00), including all kraft pulp (fluff pulp included), recycled-fiber pulp and all four recovered-paper lines (4707.10–4707.90), so they need a Commerce licence.

steps.title: File the export in AES (Electronic Export Information)
steps.whatToDo: You (the U.S. principal party in interest) or your freight forwarder file the EEI in the Automated Export System — free through ACE AESDirect — and put the confirmation number (ITN) on the shipping documents. File at least 24 hours before an ocean shipment is loaded, 2 hours before a flight departs, or 1 hour before a truck reaches the border. Not filing can cost a civil penalty of up to $17,412 per violation.
steps.when: When one Schedule B number in one shipment to one buyer is worth over $2,500, and at any value when the shipment needs a Commerce licence or a DEA permit or declaration, or ships an EAR item to Cuba, Iran, North Korea or Syria, or a Commerce Control List item to China, Russia or Venezuela.
steps.chapterNote: Pulp and recovered paper have no special filing rule: file when one Schedule B number in a shipment is worth over $2,500, and always when a licence is required. Shipments to Canada need no EEI unless a licence is required.

rules.title: Russia and Belarus: a licence is required for every Chapter 47 HS code in Supplement No. 4 to Part 746 (all except 4702.00) (15 CFR 746.8)
Recovered paper is not a hazardous waste: EPA's export rules for hazardous waste (40 CFR Part 262, Subpart H) do not apply, so no EPA export notice or consent is needed

citations.label: 40 CFR Part 262, Subpart H (transboundary movements of hazardous waste)

groups.label: Mechanical wood pulp
groups.note: Mechanical wood pulp (4701.00) is on the Russia list.

groups.label: Dissolving pulp
groups.note: No U.S. agency rule beyond the five steps; dissolving pulp is the only Chapter 47 code not on the Russia industry-sector list (Supplement No. 4).

groups.label: Kraft (sulfate) pulp: NBSK, eucalyptus, fluff
groups.note: All four kraft pulp lines (4703.11–4703.29), fluff pulp included, are on the Russia list.

groups.label: Sulfite pulp
groups.note: All four sulfite pulp lines are on the Russia list.

groups.label: Semichemical (mechanical-chemical) pulp
groups.note: Semichemical pulp (4705.00) is on the Russia list.

groups.label: Recycled-fiber, cotton linter & bamboo pulp
groups.note: Cotton linter, recycled-fiber, bamboo and other fibrous pulps (4706.10–4706.93) are all on the Russia list.

groups.label: Recovered paper (waste & scrap)
groups.note: All four recovered-paper lines are on the Russia list. No EPA export notice is needed; the buyer country's licence, inspection and contamination rules are on the Markets page.

savings.title: Claim the free-trade-agreement rate abroad
savings.saves: The partner country's tariff on qualifying U.S. goods — often 0% instead of its normal rate.
savings.appliesTo: Goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin, shipped to one of the 20 U.S. free-trade-agreement partners: Australia, Bahrain, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Jordan, Korea, Mexico, Morocco, Nicaragua, Oman, Panama, Peru and Singapore.
savings.document: A certification of origin from the exporter, producer or importer, which the buyer uses to claim the rate at import. For USMCA there is no set form, but it must contain the nine data elements in Annex 5-A.
savings.caveat: Whoever certifies must be able to back it up: for USMCA, a U.S. exporter or producer keeps origin records for at least 5 years, gives CBP a copy on request and tells buyers promptly about errors. Check the product's rule of origin and the partner's rate in the FTA Tariff Tool first.

savings.title: Get U.S. duty back on imported inputs (drawback)
savings.saves: 99% of the U.S. import duties, taxes and fees paid on goods or materials that are exported, or used to make the goods you export.
savings.appliesTo: Imported goods exported unused, and imported materials used to make an exported product (or, under the substitution rules, goods of the same kind).
savings.document: An electronic drawback claim in ACE, filed within 5 years of the import date, with the import and export records that tie the two together.
savings.caveat: Antidumping and countervailing duties are not refunded, and CBP takes no paper claims. The refund is on U.S. duties only; it does not lower the buyer's tariff.

savings.title: Have the Chinese buyer hold an exclusion from China's 2018–2019 counter-tariffs
savings.saves: China's 2018–2019 counter-tariff on the line: 5% on wood pulp (fluff and other kraft pulp, dissolving and mechanical pulp), 20% on recycled-fiber pulp (4706.20). It does not remove the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods.
savings.appliesTo: U.S. pulp sold to China. China's named exclusion lists have covered bleached softwood kraft pulp (ex 4703.21) and recycled-fiber pulp (4706.20); other lines rely on the buyer's own application under China's market-based exclusion process.
savings.document: The Chinese importer's exclusion, applied for through China's tariff exclusion process; the U.S. exporter supplies product and contract data.
savings.caveat: Exclusions are the Chinese importer's, not the exporter's, and are valid until December 31, 2026 unless extended. Recovered paper gains nothing: China bans its import.

citations.label: Tariff Commission Announcement No. 11 of 2023 (13th exclusion extension list)
White House fact sheet on the U.S.–China deal, Nov 1, 2025

savings.title: Help the Canadian buyer claim remission of Canada's surtax on dissolving pulp
savings.saves: The 50% surtax Canada charges on U.S. dissolving pulp (4702.00.00), refunded to (or not collected from) the Canadian importer.
savings.appliesTo: Dissolving pulp imported for use in Canada in the manufacture or processing of any good (section 3 of the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)), for example by a cellulose specialties or fibre plant.
savings.document: The Canadian importer's claim for remission, filed within two years of import, with records of how the pulp was used.
savings.caveat: Remission is the Canadian importer's claim, not the exporter's, and no other relief may have been claimed on the same goods. Kraft pulp and recovered paper pay no surtax, so they need nothing.

citations.label: United States Surtax Remission Order (2025), SOR/2025-122

disclaimer: This page summarizes U.S. export rules to help you find the right regulation; it is not legal advice. Rules change and depend on the exact product, buyer and destination — check the cited regulation and the agency before you ship.
